requirements.original_question: For a nonspecial E(F_p) subgroup of order r, can a coordinate-defined factor base support enough efficiently found m-point relations to make complete classical index calculus asymptotically faster than square-root search?
requirements.original_resolution: Give a parameterized family, an explicit membership and decomposition algorithm, a natural-query success estimate, and costs for relation rank, matrix solving and target recovery. For an experimental lead, freeze unseen targets and compare the measured exponent against tuned rho.
requirements.remaining: A scalable prime-field base with executable cheap membership/decomposition and a fully priced held-out crossover.
requirements.title: Can prime-field curves admit a sparse factor base with genuinely cheap decomposition?

requirements.original_question: Can one prove, or reliably characterize, how the solving degree grows with extension degree n, base dimension l and summand count m in the regimes that could improve ECDLP complexity?
requirements.original_resolution: Establish bounds for a specified formulation and monomial order, including field equations; then test held-out larger systems and retain censored queries. An m = 5 or 6 result needs its own evidence.
requirements.remaining: Growing-dimension solving-degree bounds; correct chained-system shape metadata and held-out satisfiable/infeasible queries.
requirements.title: What is the actual solving degree of binary summation systems as the parameters grow?

requirements.original_question: Can a low-degree or sparse correspondence represent addition among signed Frobenius orbits while keeping only a small certificate of relative phases?
requirements.original_resolution: Construct an exact quotient correspondence, independently lift its witnesses to curve points, and measure ordinary-query cost and independent-row yield on the same frozen base.
requirements.remaining: Compact algebraic witnesses for relative Frobenius phases, including membership, splitting and lift costs.
requirements.title: Can Frobenius orbit decomposition retain a compact algebraic witness?

requirements.original_question: Can nonlinear stable bases combine many usable subgroup points, few orbit columns and cheap membership constraints without moving the cost into auxiliary variables or phase search?
requirements.original_resolution: Compare exact point sets and encodings on identical inputs, and measure setup, auxiliary-variable count, failed-query cost, useful rank and one-target recovery. Retain the existing weight encoding as a matched control.
requirements.remaining: Scalable nonlinear algebraic membership/solving; gamma weight is not a normal-basis Hamming ideal.
requirements.title: Which Frobenius-stable nonlinear factor bases keep both yield and decomposition cost favorable?

requirements.original_question: Are there explicit quasi-subfield polynomial families at the desired prime n whose rational roots yield a usable factor base and a complete attack better than the current alternatives?
requirements.original_resolution: Supply a parameter family meeting all construction hypotheses, prove or measure its usable point count and natural success rate, and account for building the base and solving its relations.
requirements.remaining: A useful prime-degree parameter family, subgroup yield law and complete measured IC integration.
requirements.title: Can explicit quasi-subfield constructions become useful at prime extension degrees?

requirements.original_question: Can symmetric coordinates, chained S3 equations or hybrid solvers find verified ordinary m-point decompositions faster than existing methods after splitting and membership checks are charged?
requirements.original_resolution: Use independently labeled ordinary and planted corpora at increasing m and l. Count all splitting, sign, rationality, subgroup and failed-query work, and compare direct, chained and symmetric formulations on the same base.
requirements.remaining: Growing arity with full splitting/lifting/matrix costs; literal ten-summand toy results do not transfer to N83.
requirements.title: Can multi-summand formulations avoid paying back their degree reduction during lifting?

requirements.original_question: Which witness selection, partial-relation recombination and stopping policies minimize cost per new rank contribution and per independently recovered target log?
requirements.original_resolution: Freeze the query stream and rank checkpoints; compare collectors by rank gained per unit work, include partial-relation graph costs, and verify fresh-target descent. State how unavoidable kernels and anchors are handled.
requirements.remaining: Rank and descent reliability laws, optimized large-prime policies and fully priced reusable setup/online windows.
requirements.title: How can a collector buy independent rank and reliable target descent efficiently?

requirements.original_question: Can a concrete transport or correspondence produce enough cheap, independent relations to improve the DLP, including any links needed between modular isogeny classes?
requirements.original_resolution: Recheck rank modulo the actual subgroup prime, prove the appropriate kernel dimension, and charge explicit map and target-transport costs. Compare complete same-target runs rather than infer a benefit from a changed conductor or j-invariant.
requirements.remaining: Explicit paid isogeny transport and a Hecke-rank theorem or certified counterexample in its stated model.
requirements.title: Can isogeny and Hecke mechanisms overcome their rank and transport barriers?

requirements.original_question: Can a cover or Jacobian construction preserve the desired elliptic subgroup and yield cheaper relation collection and target recovery for that component?
requirements.original_resolution: Prove pullback injectivity on the chosen subgroup, provide exact norm or pushforward operations and valid target lifts, identify the required E-component rank, and price the full pipeline against elliptic rho in the original field.
requirements.remaining: Independent exact source-order proofs, a general Jacobian norm and a cheaper higher-genus relation/descent solver.
requirements.title: Can a higher-genus cover make the elliptic component cheaper to solve?

requirements.original_question: For a precisely specified family, can any current algebraic, SAT, hybrid or quantum-annealing IC method recover an unseen target faster than tuned rho under comparable resources, and does the advantage persist as size increases?
requirements.original_resolution: Run repeated same-point comparisons over a frozen size ladder and held-out tier. Report online one-target time as primary, reusable preprocessing and cold totals separately, and multi-target workloads with their own target count. For annealing, include embedding, classical preprocessing, readout and repetitions; establish scaling rather than extrapolate a small demonstration.
requirements.remaining: Wide IC at N83, N131 transfer justification, isolated A/A, independent host, complete pricing, held-out scaling and matched GPU/annealing hardware.
requirements.title: Where is the verified complete-attack crossover with tuned Pollard rho?
